CHROMIUM: config: enable RFC 4191 (icmp6 RA route info option) Android P started requiring support for RFC 4191 in Android O. This is now also a requirement for ARC++P. More specifically Android CTS now checks that the two following sysctl are defined and set to conform values as per the RFC: - net.ipv6.conf.$iface.accept_ra_rt_info_max_plen - net.ipv6.conf.$iface.accept_ra_rt_info_min_plen RFC 4191 is enabled by turning on CONFIG_IPV6_ROUTE_INFO. Doing so will allow the ipv6 stack to parse and accept Route Info options (RIOs) in icmp6 RAs received by the host. Note that by default the ra_rt_info_{max,min}_plen sysctls are set to 0 which means RIOs are not taken into account. RFC 4191 has a section w.r.t security concerns of accepting RIOs. In short accepting RIOs does not create additional attack vectors if the network did not had already some link layer security. See the RFC for details of scenarios. BUG=b:79696986 TEST=./chromeos/scripts/kernelconfig olddefconfig compiled, flashed betty, checked that files are defined in /proc/sys/net as expected. Signed-off-by: Hugo Benichi <hugobenichi@chromium.org> Change-Id: I0d4529ed3863b65948a23140d65d47688b3941d3 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1082173 Commit-Ready: Hugo Benichi <hugobenichi@google.com> Tested-by: Kirtika Ruchandani <kirtika@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Guenter Roeck <groeck@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Kirtika Ruchandani <kirtika@chromium.org>
